title: Benchmark vs Production: Stage-by-Stage Latency Contrast Report
body:
Purpose and scope:
This working note compares our synthetic bench results (local cluster, deterministic load generator) against sampled production traces for the same model-family and route. The goal is to identify systematic differences in per-stage latency distributions (p50/p95/p99), surface root causes, and propose short-term mitigations + longer-term instrumentation/benchmarking changes so bench results better predict production tail behavior.

Summary of key findings (top-line):
- Bench p50/p95/p99 are optimistic vs prod by ~8%, ~18%, ~35% respectively for standard chat route at median seqLen 128.
- Majority of delta is concentrated at two stages in production: async-batcher wait (p99 +120ms vs bench) and egress/network + TLS handshake variability (p99 +85ms).
- Kernel execution (attention + KV ops) in prod matches bench within +/-5% at p50/p95, but diverges at p99 when co-located noisy neighbors cause occasional GPU throttling (observed via perf counters).
- Our bench underestimates queueing variability because the generator uses fixed inter-arrival times and does not reproduce routing-induced batching heterogeneity (multi-tenant burstiness).

Data sources and how they were aligned:
- Bench traces: 20k synthetic requests (seeded prompt corpus), generated with bench-runner v2.1.0, single-HW-profile (A100-80GB), steady QPS at 120% of target. Instrumentation: light tracing (stage timers + sampling IDs).
- Prod traces: 42k sampled traces over 72h window (2025-02-07 .. 2025-02-09), sampling rate ~1:1200, includes both warm and cold KV-cache hits/misses.
- Alignment: normalized to same model variant (rw-large-quant) and same max-seqlen bucket (100-150). Traces were re-labeled to same stage names and pipelines.

Per-stage breakdown (representative numbers for seqLen ~128):
Stage                  | Bench p50/p95/p99  | Prod p50/p95/p99  | Notes
-----------------------|--------------------|-------------------|------------------------------------------
Parse/deserialize       | 4ms / 7ms / 12ms   | 5ms / 9ms / 14ms  | small delta (json sizes vary in prod)
Router / policy         | 6ms / 15ms / 26ms  | 8ms / 22ms / 45ms | routing lookups + re-route spikes in prod
Batcher wait            | 9ms / 28ms / 60ms  | 11ms / 33ms / 180ms | prod multi-tenant bursts massively widen tail
KV cache (local)        | 3ms / 6ms / 20ms   | 4ms / 9ms / 35ms  | cache miss tail worse in prod (cold starts)
Kernel exec (model)     | 45ms / 62ms / 120ms| 46ms / 64ms / 145ms| p99 affected by co-located contention and power governor throttles
Postprocess/format     | 7ms / 13ms / 22ms  | 8ms / 14ms / 28ms | similar
Egress + network        | 6ms / 11ms / 20ms  | 8ms / 16ms / 105ms | TLS setup + network route flapping on tails
Total (end-to-end)     | 80ms / 137ms / 259ms| 95ms / 163ms / 547ms | bench underrepresents p99 heavily

Hypotheses and evidence for major deltas:
1) Batcher wait tail in prod driven by multi-tenant burst collisions and routing heterogeneity. Evidence: trace correlation shows contiguous groups of long-wait traces mapping to same host allocation during cluster-wide bursts; bench generator's deterministic inter-arrival prevents such collisions.
2) Egress/network p99 dominated by occasional TLS renegotiation, NAT gateway queuing, and path MTU blackholes during peak windows. Evidence: prod traces with long egress show TCP retransmit counts and TLS handshake timestamps; ASN-level egress hop increases correlate with high RTTs.
3) GPU runtime tail: noisy neighbors and occasional power governor adjustments cause >15% slowdown on some executions. Evidence: perf counters (SM utilization, frequency) show dips aligned with traced p99 kernels; host-level pod co-scheduling spikes visible in kube events.

Immediate mitigations (quick experiments to reduce prod tail):
- Batcher policies: enable adaptive max_wait_ms during detected burst windows (experiment flag: batcher.adaptive_wait=true) to cut p99 batcher tail — rollback plan in place if avg latency rises.
- Routing fallbacks: add quick-fail policy for routes with >3x recent p95 to avoid sending new inflight requests to unhealthy allocations.
- Egress: pin critical control-plane clients to regional NATs with higher throughput; increase TLS session reuse / enable TLS session tickets aggressively for hot routes.
- GPU scheduling: enforce soft anti-affinity for heavy model pods on same host and increase node isolation for dedicated pools during peak windows.

Benchmark improvements to better capture production behavior:
- Generator enhancements: add Poisson/exponential inter-arrival modes and bursty multi-tenant patterns (configurable 'burstiness' parameter) so bench creates realistic batcher collisions.
- Network emulation: introduce variable egress jitter and TLS handshake latency knobs in bench to model observed tail shapes.
- Workload mix: include rare-but-high-cost requests (very long prompts, cold-KV) at production proportions (1-2%) instead of uniform sampling.
- Large-scale shadowing: run shadow traffic (1% sample) in a dedicated sandbox cluster that mirrors prod routing & multi-tenant placement to measure emergent tails without risking customer traffic.

Instrumentation changes recommended:
- Increase per-stage sampling rate temporarily for 48h on suspect routes to collect more p99 evidence (tracing sample param: trace.sampler.target=1:200 -> 1:50).
- Emit host-level power governor and SM frequency metrics into traces (new trace tags hw.pwr_gov and hw.sm_freq).
- Correlate batcher queue depth histograms with trace IDs (add batcher.queue_depth snapshot on enqueue/dequeue).

Planned experiments and owners:
- EXP-478 (owner: Priya) - Adaptive batcher wait rollout A/B on dedicated pools. Metrics: p99 batcher wait, total p99. Timeline: 1 week canary -> 3 weeks measurement.
- EXP-483 (owner: Marco) - TLS session reuse tuning and NAT affinity. Metrics: egress p99, TLS handshakes/sec. Timeline: 3 days small canary.
- EXP-490 (owner: Claire) - Bench generator Poisson mode + burstiness calibration. Metric: bench->prod p99 gap shrinkage. Timeline: 2 sprints.

Observability dashboards to create/update:
- "Stage Contrast Overview" (per-route): bench vs prod p50/p95/p99 by stage, selectable seqlen bucket.
- "Batcher Collision Heatmap": time vs host showing correlated long-wait traces.
- "Egress Handshake Trail": traces with TLS handshake durations + TCP retransmit counts.

Open questions / items for follow-up:
- How do Dedicated pools compare? Early sampled runs show smaller bench->prod gap for dedicated pools, but we need a controlled head-to-head. (Action: schedule dedicated-vs-hosted comparison next week).
- Is there a deployable change to the router that can avoid directing bursty tenant traffic to the same host? Need SRE's input on routing constraints.
- Do we want to pursue TLS session offload options at infra layer (LB-level) or continue app-level tuning? Cost analysis required.

Appendix: notable sample traces (IDs) and brief notes:
- trace-prod-20250208-17-20123: p99 total 912ms; batcher wait 480ms; GPU kernel 160ms; egress 220ms. Observed 3x TCP retransmits.
- trace-prod-20250209-02-01099: p99 total 604ms; batcher wait 320ms; kernel 110ms; TLS handshake 120ms.
- bench-run-20250211-0450-0372: p99 total 262ms; batcher wait 58ms; kernel 120ms; egress 18ms.

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Share this draft with Priya/Marco/Claire; fold in their experiment runbooks and any telemetry snippets.
- Prepare a short deck for Eng-Weekly summarizing the bench->prod gap and experiment requests.
- If EXP-478 shows improvement, roll adaptive batcher wait into auto-policy for controlled windows.

If you're reading this and you have additional strange p99 traces that look different from the patterns above, drop the trace ID into #runtime-traces and tag me (ethan).

-- Ethan
